text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parliament approves 1997/98 budget ahead of summer recess.

- Parliament approves recommendation calling on government to continue providing free medicine to non-Kuwaitis. MPs, calling recent ban a violation of human rights, say welfare state should not prohibit free medicine in public hospitals until proposed insurance scheme is introduced. Some 1.25 million expatriates live in the oil state compared with 710,000 Kuwaitis.
- Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah tells parliament: We do not differentiate between a Kuwaiti and (expatriate) resident in health services.
- Trade between South Korea and Kuwait reached $912 million in first five months of 1997.

- Kuwait and Jordan resume direct mail links. Kuwait downgraded ties and severed generous financial aid to Jordan and other Arab states it accused of siding with 1990-91 Iraqi occupation. In recent months there have been signs of rapprochement.

- Crown Prince and Prime Minister Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah fly to Paris from London for private visit. Sheikh Saad left Kuwait in March on Saudi Arabian hospital aircraft after emergency colon surgery.
- Chairman of Kuwait association for defending public funds, Mohsen al-Mutairi, criticises government for failing to approve formation of his group.
